title: Resumable mmap lazyloader and safetensors fallback
body:
Summary:

This doc proposes a resumable, device-aware mmap-backed lazy loading subsystem with a safetensors-first fallback path and an adaptive eviction/pinning policy that integrates with KV cache and the request scheduler. The goal is to reduce cold-start token latency and OOMs for large models while enabling safe hot-swap and partial weight replacement in hosted and private deployments.

Design goals and constraints:
- Minimize latency impact of first requests after model activation.
- Support interrupted loads and resumable transfers for unreliable networks and rolling restarts.
- Prefer read-only mmap where available, but fall back to streamed safetensors parsing and incremental deserialization when mmap is not viable.
- Provide per-layer, chunked placement so critical layers (attention, embeddings) can be prioritized for GPU residency.
- Integrate with KV cache metrics so eviction decisions account for per-token cache hit rates.
- Support operator-initiated hot-swap of model artifacts with version validation and safe rollback.
- Keep runtime kernel assumptions simple: layer blobs must be page-aligned for efficient mmap, quantized blobs are preferred for fallback variants.

Key concepts and components:

1) Resumable mmap-backed artifact loader (RML)
- Primary path: map the model artifact (safetensors or combined weight blob) into address space using mmap with MAP_POPULATE optional. Use advisory madvise hints for sequential or random access depending on profile.
- For cloud filesystems that do not support mmap (S3fs, some NFS configs), fall back to chunked streaming.
- The loader exposes a small state machine per-blob: UNINITIALIZED -> MAPPED -> VALIDATED -> ACTIVATED. State must persist to local checkpoint file so process restarts can resume.
- Resume strategy: maintain a small load-checkpoint that records which byte ranges were verified (checksums) and which page ranges are resident. On restart, continue verification and mapping from the last confirmed offset. This reduces rework on flaky transfers.

2) Safetensors-first fallback path
- When mmap is unavailable or the artifact is a safetensors archive that must be parsed, use an incremental safetensors parser that emits per-tensor chunks. Each tensor chunk is stored into an on-disk cache file aligned to OS page boundaries. That file is then mmaped for the same memory semantics as the primary path.
- Parser must validate tensor shape/dtype metadata before mapping chunks to avoid wasted disk writes.
- If safetensors archive contains quantized variants and fp16 variants, prefer the quantized variant where device supports (permits correct kernels) to reduce memory footprint.

3) Per-layer chunking and prioritization
- Split weight artifacts into logical chunks: embeddings, attention weights (q/k/v, out), MLP weights, layernorm/bias. Chunks are the unit of residency and eviction.
- Prioritization policy defaults: embeddings > first N transformer layers > attention q/k/v weights > layernorm > MLP out projections. Policy configurable via profile (latency-sensitive vs throughput-oriented).
- The scheduler reports per-request access frequencies to the residency controller to adjust priorities dynamically.

4) Adaptive pinning and soft-eviction
- Pinning: keep a small set of chunks pinned on GPU memory for models with steady traffic. Pinning decisions are driven by a score: access_frequency * layer_importance / memory_cost. Periodically recompute scores and adjust pinned set.
- Soft-eviction: before forcibly evicting a chunk, attempt to evict a least-likely chunk or migrate to CPU memory using a compressed (quantized) variant if available. Migration path: GPU -> CPU (pinned), mark as cold, and defer full page writeback until quiet window.
- Hard eviction (immediate unmap) is allowed for emergency OOMs, but requires request scheduler to gracefully reject or route to fallback model variant.

5) KV cache-aware decisions
- Runtime exposes per-token KV cache hit/miss rates per model variant. Residency controller factors KV cache effectiveness in pinning score since KV hits reduce re-access to base weights. High KV-hit models may tolerate more aggressive eviction.
- A special mode (kv-affinity) pins attention projection matrices when KV misses rise above threshold since re-computing these layers yields high token latency.

6) Resumable streaming protocol and checksums
- Artifact uploads for private deployments and internal model registry must include a lightweight manifest: chunk offsets, SHA256 per chunk, total size, and optional signed metadata (build id, quantization profile).
- During streaming, each chunk is written to a temporary backing file and validated against chunk checksum before being promoted to the active blob. The promotion step is atomic via rename to ensure other processes don't see partially-written blobs.
- Loader supports range-requests to resume from last good chunk; transfers use exponential backoff and range verification.

7) Hot-swap and safe-activation protocol
- Hot-swap is a two-phase commit: prepare and activate.
- Prepare: download/stream new artifact, validate manifest, build per-chunk checksums, compute compatibility matrix (e.g., kernel compatibility, quantization compatibility). Keep existing model active.
- Activate: atomically switch the model pointer in the serving layer and mark old artifact as candidate for eviction after a cool-off period. Activation must fail if compatibility checks fail.
- Rollback: if errors occur within activation cool-off, revert pointer to previous artifact and resume pinned set restoration.

8) Metrics and observability
- Expose metrics: chunk_load_time_seconds, chunk_validate_seconds, chunk_resume_count, pinned_chunks_total, eviction_count_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio, model_activation_time_seconds, hot_swap_success_total, hot_swap_rollback_total.
- Traces should correlate request ids to residency events (which chunk triggered a page-in) to aid latency investigations.
- Alerting rules: frequent resumptions or high chunk_resume_count indicate storage instability; high eviction_count_total coincident with latency spikes indicates pinning policy misconfiguration.

9) Operator controls and tooling
- CLI: model-load-inspect model_name --show-pinned, --show-residency, --force-evict chunk_id, --pin chunk_id, --promote-artifact /path/to/artifact.manifest
- Web console surfaces per-model residency heatmap by layer and allows manual pin/unpin and hot-swap triggers with before/after diff of manifests.

10) Testing strategy
- Unit tests for incremental safetensors parser and checksum validation.
- Integration tests: simulated S3 failures, partial downloads, and resumed transfers verifying final checksum and activation.
- Chaos tests: random process restarts during streaming, constrained memory budgets to force eviction paths, and hot-swap during peak traffic.
- Performance tests: compare cold-start token latency with and without prioritized pinning across model sizes (7B, 13B, 34B).

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): Enable RML on a small fleet for internal models with FS that supports mmap. Monitor chunk_resume_count and cold-start p50.
- Phase 2: Enable safetensors incremental parser and streaming fallback for S3-backed artifacts. Expand to dedicated and private clusters with feature flag.
- Phase 3: Enable hot-swap and operator tooling, run canary hot-swaps on non-critical model endpoints.

Backward compatibility notes:
- Keep legacy streaming loader as opt-in fallback for customers with bespoke model formats.
- Provide a conversion utility that produces page-aligned blob files and manifest metadata to maximize mmap compatibility for customer-supplied artifacts.

Open questions and risks:
- How to handle shared GPU memory across multiple tenants when multiple models want the same pinned chunks? (multi-tenant pin arbitration needed)
- Checksum overhead vs. startup latency: need to tune chunk sizes to balance verification time and resumability granularity.
- Interaction with kernel-level memory pressure: madvise hints are advisory; need fallback heuristics when kernel aggressively reclaims pages.

Appendix: config knobs (names are tentative)
- loader.chunk_size_bytes: default 16MB
- loader.resume_checkpoint_path: /var/lib/redwood/loader-checkpoints
- residency.pin_score_decay_half_life_seconds: 600
- residency.max_pinned_bytes_per_model: 6GB
- loader.mmap_populate: true|false
- safetensors.parser.prefetch_workers: 2
- hot_swap.cool_off_seconds: 300

Example minimal manifest snippet (human readable):
- model: tiny-llm-v1
- artifact_size: 24_576_000_000
- chunks: [list of offsets and sha256s]
- variant: int8|fp16
- created_by: ci-build-234

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus review on resumability semantics and safety of hot-swap activation.
- Check that per-chunk atomic promotion prevents races with concurrent readers.
- Validate that the adaptive pinning formula is practical for models with uneven layer costs (e.g., extremely wide MLPs).

Next steps:
- Prototype incremental safetensors parser and chunk-backed mmap file promotion.
- Instrument residency controller with initial pinning score and test on 13B internal model.
- Build CLI inspect tooling and a minimal hot-swap prepare/activate flow for operator testing.
